note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure.” That is what Jonathan was to David.

“Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.” The Philistines could not get him, so now he wants Israelites to kill an Israelite; that is how far down the slope this man has gone. “But Jonathan Saul’s son delighted much in David”, and told him, “Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself.”

Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne. You would think his loyalty lay with his daddy, but he saw the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. His loyalty exceeded his own desires. That is the kind of friend to look for, and the lesson to learn from Jonathan.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.” That is the law in the book, and Saul was set on breaking it.

Jonathan put it before his father: “Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works have been to thee-ward very good.” David “did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine”, and Saul saw it “and didst rejoice.” So “wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?”

Without a cause: in chapter 18 it was just a feeling, wrath at David for nothing. As Christ explained in the spirit, that anger without a cause leads to actually wanting to murder, which is why it carries the same judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.” That is the boat Saul put himself in when he sought to “sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause.”

For that moment Saul heard it: “Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain.” And Jonathan brought David to Saul, “and he was in his presence, as in times past.”

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.” That is what Michal was to David that night.

Saul “sent messengers unto David’s house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning.” Having tried to turn his son against David, he now leans on his daughter, David's own wife. But Michal warned him: “If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.” She “let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.”

She laid an image in the bed with “a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster”, and told the messengers, “He is sick.” Saul said, “Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him”, and they found the image. Michal covered herself, saying David threatened her, “Let me go; why should I kill thee?”, but she was looking out for her husband.

At this time Michal was a righteous example, a ride or die. She turns sour some chapters down the line, but here she saved his life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.”

Note Saul's words: “Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped?” Saul and David were brothers, both Israel, Benjamin and Judah. Saul made his brother his enemy, and David loved him anyway. That is the understanding Christ was going into: David exemplified it with Saul.
